action.description: enable, disable, delete, reset_usage, add_group, remove_group, set_quota, set_expiry or set_device_limit.

value.description: The group name, the quota (an object with quota_bytes and quota_period), the expiry in Unix seconds or null, or the device limit.

revision.description: The revision the change was made on, which the node checks as If-Match.
The revision the node's config was last read at, which the change is applied on.

typed.description: The eight groups the other operator reads out. Typing this side's own does not confirm.

key_origin.description: "device" when the device made its key, "panel" when the panel did. The second is the weaker choice: the private key sits in the panel's database and travels in the document.

token_gen.description: The link generation the device enrolled with.

passphrase.description: At least 12 characters. It cannot be recovered: a backup without it is useless.

file.description: The same as the content of a file the client imports.

link.description: A whole signed document in a link, when it is small enough for one. Null otherwise.

public_key.description: The WireGuard public key of the inbound.

transport_public_key.description: The public half of the node transport key. Null when the inbound has none.

cert.description: Paths of the certificate and key files on the node. Needed for vless and trojan, refused for shadowsocks.

decoy.description: For vless and trojan, the origin of the operator's own web server (http://127.0.0.1:8080) that anything that is not a user's connection is handed to. Taken from the node's `tls` transport when left out; the inbound is refused when the node has none.

host.description: The host the links name, in the place of the node's first public address.

listen.description: The address Xray listens on. 0.0.0.0 when left out.

qr_svg.description: The same link as an SVG QR code.

veilway.description: The link in the form providers hand out. A secret: it is shown to the one who asked and stored nowhere but in the sealed copy.

Live.description: What the last poll saw, for the pages that show the node now.

exits.description: Every exit with its state: whether its proxy relays UDP, whether its interface is up, whether its link is up.

health.description: Version, uptime, generation, flows and the counters that say the node is unwell.

rates.description: Rates in bytes per second over the node's window, by user, inbound, exit and outbound.

allowed_sources.description: Source addresses the token works from. Empty means any.

scope.description: "read" (reads only), "users" (users, devices and links) or "full" (everything an API token may do).

NodeState.description: Whether the node took the change. The panel's database is changed either way and the next successful push brings the node up to date.

NotFound.description: What the endpoint (and every path the panel does not serve) answers to a request it will not take. The operator copies it from the web server in front, see "The endpoint" on the subscription format page.

direction.description: "forward" or "reverse". In a forward link this node is the exit.

inbound.description: The tag of the `veilway` inbound the link connects to.

inbound_public_key.description: The inbound's WireGuard public key, as `/links/inbounds` reports it.

tag.description: The tag the link gets in this node's config.

transport_public_key.description: Needed when `transports` lists tls or ws.

transports.description: The transports the other node is offered, in the shape of a profile's `transports`.

set.description: Members that replace the derived ones, such as `inbound_public_key`, `name` or `transports`. An empty object clears the override.

accept.description: Must be true: the operator has seen where this node would dial and agrees.

tag.description: The tag the link gets in this node's config.

remove_devices.description: Remove the devices that were enrolled with the old link. They are listed in the answer either way.

saved_as.description: The folder in the data directory that holds the database and keys this restore replaced.

value.description: The new content of the section: a list for inbounds, outbounds and exits, an object for routing.

Settings.description: What an operator sets once for the whole panel.

endpoint_pins.description: SHA-256 of the SubjectPublicKeyInfo of the endpoint's certificate, standard base64, when it has no certificate from an authority. The first is put in links. Empty for a chain-validated endpoint.

endpoint_url.description: The public `https` URL of the subscription endpoint, with the path the web server forwards to the panel's `sub_path`. No fragment.

node_host.description: The public host or address of this node, which the profiles' endpoints are made with.

not_found.description: What the endpoint answers to a request it will not take, instead of the config file's. Null keeps the file's.

pool_v4.description: The address pool devices get their tunnel address from, an IPv4 network.

profile_overrides.description: Edits to the profiles derived from the node's inbounds, by inbound tag: an object whose members replace the derived ones.

profiles.description: One profile per inbound, in the shape of "A profile" on the subscription format page, without `device`. The panel adds the device.

refresh_mirrors.description: Other endpoints of the same subscription, put in every document as `refresh_urls`. A string, or an object with `url` and `pins`.

show_links_once.description: Store no copy of a token: a link is shown at creation and reset, and never again.

start_id.description: Different on every start of the server.

can_show.description: Whether the panel holds a sealed copy, so the link can be shown again. False with "show links once".

key_fingerprints.description: Fingerprints of the current signing keys, which are not secret.

token.description: Shown once. Only its hash is stored.

totp_secret.description: Base32, for an authenticator app. Shown once.

can_update.description: Whether the folder for update requests exists, which a host installed or updated by `veilway.sh` has.

latest.description: The newest release, when it is newer than this panel.

updating.description: A request was made and this panel has not come back as another version yet.

device_limit.description: 0 is no limit beyond the node's own 16.

exits.description: "all" or a list of exit tags.

node.description: The node's own record of the user: usage, denial and traffic. Null when the node cannot be reached.

certificate_missing.description: A vless or trojan inbound without certificate files, which the node refuses.

managed.description: Whether the panel made this inbound and holds its credentials, which links need.

link.description: A secret, like the subscription link.

qr_svg.description: The same link as an SVG QR code.

info.description: HTTP and JSON under the panel's path prefix. A browser logs in and sends the CSRF token on every change. An integration sends an API token as a Bearer header. The x-access member of an operation says what it needs: read, users or full are token scopes, session and session-reauth are for a logged-in admin only, and public needs nothing.
